title: The Manirung Pass
alt: Small figures cross a snowy valley between steep Himalayan ridges
caption: 1860s. Albumen silver print from glass negative. Met 2005.100.499 (99). The museum dates the photograph to the 1860s and identifies the expedition as 1866. Its production depended on porters, glass plates, chemicals and a portable darkroom. The image is a selected colonial view, not a neutral survey of every Himalayan community. Reproduced without cropping.
credit: Samuel Bourne; The Metropolitan Museum of Art; Gilman Collection, Purchase, Cynthia Hazen Polsky Gift, 2005
license: Public Domain / The Met Open Access (CC0)

title: The Teppa-kulam
alt: Temple towers and trees reflected in a tank behind a stone balustrade
caption: 1858. Albumen silver print from waxed paper negative. Met 2005.100.381.1.4. Linnaeus Tripe photographed this temple tank in 1858 as a government photographer in the Madras Presidency. Compare his architectural survey with Bourne's later Himalayan image; this is not a photograph by Bourne. Reproduced without cropping.
credit: Linnaeus Tripe; The Metropolitan Museum of Art; Gilman Collection, Purchase, Cynthia Hazen Polsky Gift, 2005
license: Public Domain / The Met Open Access (CC0)

title: Bhide Wada, photographed in 2021
alt: Weathered Bhide Wada facade above street shops and pedestrians
caption: A modern view of the Pune site associated with the Phules' girls' school. It records the site in 2021, not the classroom in 1848; later memorial redevelopment must not be confused with this photograph. Photograph: 2021-09-29 09:40:02. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus: facade detail
alt: Carved stone facade, clock and central dome of the Mumbai terminus
caption: A modern view of the later nineteenth-century terminus. Its stone carving and architectural detail belong to a building programme begun in 1878; it is not the station appearance at the first Bombay-Thane service in 1853. Photograph: 2011-01-07. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Mumbai terminus illuminated at night
alt: Central dome of the terminus lit orange against the night sky
caption: The modern illumination belongs to the photograph, not the nineteenth-century construction. Compare the overall facade with the detail view while separating the building's heritage role from the history of railway labour and finance. Photograph: 23 November 2022 (according to Exif data). Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Lucknow Residency entrance after the rebellion
alt: Damaged arched gateway and rubble at the Lucknow Residency
caption: Felice Beato, c. 1858; Wellcome 574503i. This photograph shows damage after the fighting. It is neither an image of the 1856 annexation nor a photograph taken during combat. Its colonial viewpoint should be compared with rebel proclamations and local testimony. Reproduced without further cropping.
credit: Felice Beato / Wellcome Collection / Wikimedia Commons

title: Indigo factory, Bengal: a published representation
alt: Workers, carts, processing vats and a smoking chimney at an indigo factory
caption: William Simpson, Indigo factory, Bengal, watercolour, 1863 (British Library WD 1017). The downloaded Commons record calls this the 1867 chromolithograph, but the visible signed watercolour corresponds to WD 1017. It postdates the 1859-60 revolt. Vats, transport and labour are visible; the orderly composition does not establish fair working conditions. Reproduced without cropping.
captureDate: 1863 watercolour; Commons description conflates it with the 1867 print

title: Delegates to the first Congress meeting, Bombay, 1885
alt: Congress delegates arranged in rows beneath a verandah in 1885
caption: The source identifies the group as delegates to the first Indian National Congress session in Bombay, 1885. The photographer is unrecorded. A formal group portrait documents a gathering, not the full social composition of later nationalist movements; individual names require a verified key. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Indian soldier cooking in France, c. 1914-15
alt: An Indian soldier crouches beside a cooking pot, with another man behind him
caption: Bain News Service; Library of Congress LC-DIG-ggbain-17577, dated c. 1914-15. Everyday food preparation is part of military service. The catalogue does not identify this soldier's name or unit; neither is invented here. Reproduced without further cropping.
credit: Bain News Service, publisher / Wikimedia Commons

title: Entrance to Jallianwala Bagh, photographed in 2018
alt: Modern Jallianwala Bagh entrance wall and commemorative statue
caption: A modern view of the commemorative site at Amritsar, not a photograph of the firing on 13 April 1919. Conservation and memorial features belong to later phases. The inquiry records remain essential for interpreting the event. Photograph: 2018-05-04. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Gandhi during the salt protest, April 1930
alt: Gandhi bends toward the ground while a group watches
caption: A widely reproduced salt-protest photograph. The Commons file labels it Dandi, 5 April; that day-level caption conflicts with sources dating the breaking of the salt law at Dandi to 6 April. The image is presented as April 1930 context, not proof of an exact day or location. The photographer remains unidentified. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Later memorial to Kanaklata Baruah
alt: Painted memorial statue of Kanaklata Barua holding a flag
caption: A modern commemorative sculpture photographed in 2017, recalling Kanaklata Baruah's role in the Quit India movement in Assam. It is not an eyewitness photograph of the 1942 procession. An identified local record and testimony remain requested. Photograph: 2017-02-01 21:28:39. Reproduced without further cropping.

title: Ram Mohan Roy: an early nineteenth-century portrait
alt: Painted bust portrait of Ram Mohan Roy in a red robe and patterned turban
caption: V&A portrait record O16865, dated around 1820 in the image catalogue; artist unidentified. This likeness is not an illustration of a sati ceremony or the 1829 regulation. Legal change, reform advocacy and women's experiences require different sources. Reproduced without further cropping.
credit: Unidentified artist / Victoria and Albert Museum / Wikimedia Commons

title: Indian Independence Act 1947: opening page
alt: Opening page of the Indian Independence Act with its 18 July 1947 date
caption: The Act received royal assent on 18 July 1947 and provided for two independent Dominions from 15 August. This is the opening page, not the full Act, the Radcliffe boundary award or a record of refugee experiences. Open the official text for the complete provisions. Reproduced without further cropping.
credit: Government of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland / Wikimedia Commons

title: The Santhal Hul through the colonial illustrated press
alt: Press illustration of armed men searching huts beside an elephant
caption: Published in The Illustrated London News, 23 February 1856. This scene of a search for rebels represents a British newspaper's framing of the uprising; it is not a photograph or a participant's account. The historical caption uses the colonial spelling Santhal. Reproduced without further cropping.
credit: The Illustrated London News; engraver unidentified / Wikimedia Commons

title: Nehru and Gandhi at the Bombay Congress meeting, 1942
alt: Nehru and Gandhi seated together with papers in front of them
caption: The catalogue identifies the scene as the All-India Congress Committee meeting in Bombay on 8 August 1942. It documents leadership at a meeting, not a street protest or the experiences of all regional participants. Reproduced without further cropping.
credit: Unidentified photographer; W. W. Norton reproduction / Wikimedia Commons

title: Laying rails on the Bhore Ghaut, c. 1855-62
alt: Railway viaduct under construction across a rocky hillside
caption: William Johnson; Southern Methodist University, DeGolyer Library. The photograph shows construction after the opening of the Bombay-Thane passenger service. Workers and the difficult terrain belong in the railway story; this is not a photograph of the first train in 1853. Reproduced without further cropping.
credit: William Johnson; Southern Methodist University, Central University Libraries, DeGolyer Library / Wikimedia Commons

title: Queen Victoria's proclamation, 1858
alt: Three printed pages of the 1858 proclamation with handwritten annotations
caption: A reduced reproduction of the proclamation associated with the transfer to Crown rule. The surviving image is not a substitute for a readable complete text. Distinguish the proclamation's promises from the Government of India Act and from later implementation. Reproduced without further cropping.
credit: British Crown proclamation; reproduction via Moving Here archive / Wikimedia Commons

title: Eastern Bengal and Assam with Bhutan: Imperial Gazetteer map
alt: Gazetteer map labelled Eastern Bengal and Assam with Bhutan
caption: Imperial Gazetteer mapping published 1907-09, after the partition of Bengal in 1905. Historical administrative boundaries and names are retained; they are not present-day national borders. Read the printed legend and consult the larger source image for small labels. The map does not depict the partition of India in 1947.
credit: J. G. Bartholomew / Imperial Gazetteer of India; Digital South Asia Library reproduction via Wikimedia Commons
